security_audit.summary: All 59 static alerts were false positives caused by Markdown delimiters, inline code, expected Azure endpoints, environment configuration, and audio decoding. Semantic review found two concerns: generic function dispatch lacks shown allowlisting, and examples print session or transcript data. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, obfuscated payload, or automatic command execution was found.

remediation.issue: The function-calling example dispatches service-provided names and arguments through a generic handler.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist tool names, validate arguments against strict schemas, enforce authorization, and reject unknown functions before executing application actions.

remediation.issue: Examples print complete session details and voice transcripts.
remediation.suggestion: Disable content logging by default, redact sensitive fields, document retention controls, and restrict access to production logs.

content.user_title: Build Real-Time Azure Voice AI Apps
content.value_statement: Real-time voice applications require careful coordination of authentication, audio streaming, events, and turn handling. This skill provides focused Python patterns for Azure AI Voice Live workflows.
actual_capabilities: Configure asynchronous Voice Live connections with DefaultAzureCredential or an Azure API key.
Stream base64-encoded PCM or G.711 audio through input and output buffers.
Handle session, transcription, audio, response, function-call, and error events.
Configure server-based or Azure semantic voice activity detection.
Manage interruptions, manual turns, conversation history, voices, and audio formats.
limitations: The skill provides documentation and snippets, not a complete executable application.
Usage requires an Azure endpoint, valid credentials, service access, and compatible model deployment.
Microphone capture, audio playback, tool handlers, and production infrastructure remain implementation responsibilities.
The referenced supplementary files are not included in the audited package.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Create an authenticated Python prototype that streams speech and receives spoken responses.

use_cases.title: Add Voice to Support Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan turn detection, interruption handling, transcripts, and approved function calls for customer conversations.

use_cases.title: Connect Telephony Audio
use_cases.description: Select G.711 or PCM formats and manual turn controls for an existing call platform.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal Azure AI Voice Live Python connection using DefaultAzureCredential. Explain the required environment variable and each session option.

prompt_templates.title: Stream Microphone Audio
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an asynchronous audio loop for 24 kHz mono PCM16. Include input buffering, response audio handling, and clean connection shutdown.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Natural Turns
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure server voice activity detection and interruption handling for a voice assistant. Explain threshold, padding, silence, cancellation, and buffer clearing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Tool Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Voice Live function calling for these approved tools: [TOOLS]. Validate arguments, authorize actions, reject unknown names, and return structured results.

output_examples.input: Plan a basic voice assistant that uses Azure identity and the alloy voice.
output: Connection plan using the configured Azure endpoint and default identity credentials.
Session plan covering text and audio modalities, the alloy voice, and server turn detection.
Event plan for transcripts, audio responses, completion, and connection errors.

output_examples.input: Explain how to support interruptions during a spoken response.
output_examples.output: Listen for the speech-started event, cancel the active response, and clear buffered output audio before processing the new user turn.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential and grant only the service permissions required by the application.
Validate audio formats, event types, function names, and function arguments before processing.
Handle cancellation, connection closure, service errors, and resource cleanup in every streaming workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Azure keys, endpoints containing secrets, or production credentials in source files.
Do not execute model-requested functions without allowlisting, schema validation, and application authorization.
Do not log raw transcripts, session objects, or audio unless privacy and retention controls are established.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential for production when possible. API keys are supported, but require stricter secret storage and rotation.

faq.question: Which audio formats are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers 24 kHz PCM16, lower-rate PCM16 variants, G.711 mu-law, and G.711 A-law.

faq.question: Does the skill capture microphone audio?
faq.answer: No. It shows where audio chunks enter the workflow, but your application must implement capture and playback.

faq.question: Can I support user interruptions?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cancel the current response and clear pending output when new speech begins.

faq.question: Does it include secure function execution?
faq.answer: It demonstrates the event flow only. Your application must add tool allowlists, argument validation, authorization, and failure handling.

faq.question: Is this a complete production reference?
faq.answer: No. Add testing, observability, privacy controls, retry policies, deployment configuration, and environment-specific validation.
